# Draft:Dilawar Aimaq

General Dilawar Aimaq (, born April 5, 1963, in Nahrin District, Baghlan Province, Afghanistan) is an Afghan general, politician, and tribal leader. He is a prominent representative of the Aimaq ethnic group and served as a member of the Wolesi Jirga, the lower house of the Afghan parliament, from 2010 to 2018.
Early Life
Aimaq was born in 1963 in Baghlan Province, the son of Shir Mohammad Aimaq. He attended school in Nahrin and graduated in 1982 from the Military Academy (Harbi Pohantun) in Kabul. During the 1980s, he served as an officer in the 20th Division of the Afghan Army under the PDPA regime.
During the Afghan civil war, he supported Ahmad Shah Massoud in the resistance against the Soviet invasion. In the years following the fall of the Taliban, he was active in combating their resurgence.
Political Career
From 2010 to 2020, Dilawar Aimaq was a member of the Afghan Parliament representing Baghlan Province. He served as deputy chairman of the Internal Security Commission () and focused on security issues as well as tribal affairs. He is considered to be affiliated with the Islamic-democratic party Jamiat-e Islami.
Aimaq was also outspoken about the threat posed by the Taliban, warning between 2015 and 2017 of their growing influence in northern Afghanistan.
Personal Life
General Aimaq speaks both Dari and Pashto. He continues to live in Afghanistan and remains politically and socially active as a tribal leader.
